title: Machine learning derives a mortality risk score after traumatic spinal cord injury
summary: Using registry data from 1245 people with acute traumatic spinal cord injury, machine learning built the Spinal Cord Injury Risk Score (SCIRS) from age, neurological level and completeness, AOSpine morphology and Abbreviated Injury Scale scores (derivation n=849). In an independent validation cohort (n=396), 1-year mortality AUC was 0.86 for SCIRS versus 0.71 for the Injury Severity Score, and in-hospital mortality AUC was 0.85 versus 0.70. The study is a retrospective review of a prospective cohort, and the authors call for further validation before clinical use.
ai_technology: Machine learning models trained on registry data to derive the Spinal Cord Injury Risk Score
organization: University of British Columbia Hospital; Praxis Spinal Cord Institute; University of British Columbia

evidence.unknown: Reliability in larger independent datasets and value for clinical decision-making; full text not reviewed.
